title: Open-source tool for unpacking stripped Android native (.so) malware: static RegisterNatives recovery, ARM64 OLLVM (BR X8) deobfuscation, and Dobby anti-Frida tracing
content_md:
If you analyze Android banking trojans, droppers, or spyware, you've probably run into samples where: classes*.dex declares native methods, but lib/*.so has 0 exported Java_* symbols and wiped ELF section headers. JNI_OnLoad constructs strings on the stack ( MOVZ / MOVK ), uses an OLLVM CSEL + BR X8 state machine, and registers JNI handlers dynamically. Attaching Frida immediately crashes the app due to /proc/self/maps or libc prologue checks. I released JNISleuth-MCP (Apache 2.0) to automate this part of Android malware triage: https://github.com/nighthawkk/JNISleuth-MCP Recovers static JNINativeMethod triplets from .rodata / .data.rel.ro (with PT_LOAD fallback for section-stripped ELFs). Extracts MOVZ / MOVK stack strings and XOR-encoded C2 strings from JNI_OnLoad / .init_array . Resolve
